title: Plasma mirror self-focusing boosts gamma-ray generation
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01993-1

One approach to generate high-energy X-rays and γ-rays is inverse Compton scattering, where a high-energy electron beam collides with an intense laser pulse. However, this process is notoriously difficult because the electron and laser beams must be precisely aligned in space and time. Now, a coated plasma mirror is shown to dramatically increase the efficiency and energy of the generation.

title: A milestone toward exawatt plasma optics by Raman amplification
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01989-x

Exawatt-to-zettawatt lasers are essential in the quest for an ultimate understanding of nature, but they are held back by the damage limits of conventional optics. A recent experiment of Raman pulse compression to terawatt power revitalizes the prospect of plasma-based optics for next-generation ultraintense lasers.

title: The state and prospects of the European photonics sector
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02002-1

At the centre of Europe’s rich photonics ecosystem, the European Photonics Industry Consortium (EPIC) connects stakeholders and promotes collective actions and advocacy. Nature Photonics spoke to its Director General Carlos Lee about recent trends, strengths and challenges facing Europe.

title: Doped germanium keeps pace with the light field
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01983-3

Attosecond transient reflection spectroscopy reveals that doped germanium can retain a light-field-driven sub-cycle optical response, with impurity doping shifting and reshaping electron dynamics on attosecond timescales.

title: Optical hydrogen sensing across scales
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01986-0

An optofluidic microcavity combined with an adaptive laser-locking scheme makes it possible to monitor hydrogen from individual molecules to per cent-level concentrations with a compact device.

title: Fluid motion and crystallization control enable air-processed fully screen-printed perovskite solar cells
abstract:
Nature Photonics, Published online: 27 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01991-3

Solvent engineering optimizes fluid motion and crystallization in fully screen-printed perovskite solar cells, resulting in devices with a certified power conversion efficiency of 21.86%, 90.5% of which is maintained after 2,000 h of operation.
